claim_being_audited: That rejecting Kestrel-Borderline-012 is compliant because admissible due-diligence evidence shows a material unresolved risk from an unresolved storage-control variance combined with weak process documentation.
specific_concerns: The policy requires admissible evidence of a material unresolved risk for rejection, but the packet shows a questionnaire inconsistency and informal quality documentation without clearly establishing materiality.
BPROC-012-E supports follow-up before approval if storage controls remain unresolved; it does not itself direct rejection.
BPROC-012-D expressly notes no failed control test is logged, which undercuts any implication of a proven control failure.

The packet is careful not to claim a confirmed security failure, but it still moves from follow-up/escalation evidence to a reject decision without a clearly documented link showing that the unresolved issue remained material at decision time.
unsupported_claims: Any claim that the record proves a reject-level control failure.
Any claim that storage controls were definitively noncompliant rather than unresolved/inconsistent.
Any claim that the cited evidence expressly required rejection rather than follow-up or escalation.
evidence_requests: A formally logged determination that the storage-control variance remained unresolved at the time of decision.
A documented materiality/risk assessment explaining why the unresolved variance rose to reject-level risk under procurement policy.
Any admissible approval criteria, threshold, or reviewer note showing that failure to resolve this issue bars vendor approval.
Any formally logged follow-up results or lack of response from the vendor on the storage-control issue.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence satisfies the policy threshold for rejection: a material unresolved risk.
Questionnaire inconsistencies and informal quality-process documentation can justify follow-up or escalation, but do not alone prove reject-level failure under the policy text.
Do not credit unstated private security-review conclusions or inferred control failures not formally logged.
Assess whether the actor's packet stays within what the cited evidence actually establishes.
